A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PREFDISCO research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 21 models across ten tasks, including alignment scores, task accuracy, controlled interaction-length experiments, and human annotation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Table 2, Figures 3–5, and Appendices B–C. Results retained from v1 still qualify.

M1.justification: The persona construction, preference modeling, rubric evaluation, and baseline/discovery/oracle procedures remain unchanged. The added prompt templates document implementation; they do not establish a revision to the evaluated method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten benchmarks spanning mathematical, logical, scientific, factual, and social reasoning. Appendix D adds a collaborative-user prompt, but no corresponding evaluation establishes expanded scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The same 21 OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude models participate in the same baseline/discovery/oracle comparisons. The new benchmark comparison table describes related work rather than adding experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 2.3 revises the stated grading range from [0,1] to [0,5], correcting the metric specification. Both versions already describe 1–5 rubrics in Section 3. Sampling, model settings, and interaction budgets remain unchanged; the correction does not establish rescoring or reruns.

E4.justification: The questioning and accuracy analyses, fixed 2/4/8-question experiment, human validation, and six qualitative examples are retained. New prompt documentation and discussion do not introduce additional ablations or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: The Figure 3 confidence band and reported correlation significance remain unchanged, as does the human agreement analysis. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All 210 main-table scores, plotted results, and Appendix C outcomes are unchanged. Section 5 newly highlights older Claude 3-Opus outperforming Sonnet-4 on some tasks; MATH normalized alignment is 7.7 versus 2.6 in both tables. This adds an explicit qualitative finding without new numerical evidence.

T1.justification: The grading function's formal range changes from [0,1] to [0,5] in Section 2.3. The weighted alignment definition, normalization equation, preference representation, and sequential decision formulation otherwise remain unchanged; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly presents PREFALIGN as a separate contribution in the abstract and introduction, although the metric already existed in v1. New Table 1 also asserts a unique combination of benchmark properties. The central personalization claims and headline findings remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 links older-model advantages to possible RL-induced diversity loss and adds a plateau interpretation of Figure 5 to justify the five-turn limit. These extend interpretation of existing evidence. The limitations concerning simulated users, communication preferences, and harmful personalization remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly identifies the GPT-4.1 judge and its sampling settings, including temperature 0.1 and 4096 maximum tokens. New Appendices D–F disclose user-simulation, assistant-mode, preference-generation, rubric-generation, and scoring prompts. This substantially expands documentation of the central evaluation implementation.

R1.justification: New Table 1 compares PREFDISCO with PersoBench, PrefEval, PersonaMem, and UserBench across five properties. Murthy et al. and Shao et al. are added to support the RL/diversity discussion. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and publication header change, proactive personalization receives greater emphasis, and the abstract and contribution list receive localized edits. Clarifications, acknowledgments, and prompt appendices are added, while the main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the benchmark comparison table and boxed prompt displays, revises Figure 1's scenario wording, and reflows existing material. Figure 5 moves beside related work, and some appendix tables break differently across pages. Existing empirical displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The judge configuration and prompt appendices make the evaluation substantially easier to inspect and reproduce, while the grading-range correction improves consistency. The empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the added RL and interaction-plateau explanations lack additional direct validation. The net gain is a clear but limited improvement in transparency and clarity.
